title: stackvo.json (project manifest) — contract v1
description: Per-project manifest living at projects/<name>/stackvo.json. Frozen contract shared by the Bash CLI generator and the StackVo Desktop (Tauri) app. Derived from core/cli/lib/generators/project/config-parser.sh and core/ui/server/services/ProjectService.js.

name.description: Project identifier. Must match the containing directory name. Pattern is the SAFE_NAME regex enforced by core/ui/server/utils/exec.js (no shell metacharacters, no path traversal). Dots are allowed but are replaced with dashes for Traefik router names (sanitize_project_name_for_traefik).

domain.description: REQUIRED. The generator aborts the project with log_error when this is missing — there is no fallback. Convention is <name>.loc. Must have a matching /etc/hosts entry pointing at 127.0.0.1.

runtime.description: Canonical runtime id. ABSENT MEANS 'php' — readers MUST apply that default, because all pre-v1 PHP projects on disk omit this key. Writers MUST emit it explicitly. php and node have Bash generators; python, go, ruby, rust, bun and deno are generated by the desktop app's Rust engine only (C-02, closed app-side in Sprint 18). bun and deno are JavaScript runtimes but are NOT the 'node' runtime: they read the same package.json and are built from their own images with their own verbs, so treating them as a node variant would mean one block whose meaning depended on a sibling key. See runtimeAliases in CONFLICTS.md for the accepted-on-read legacy spellings ('golang' is corrected to 'go' on read).

server.description: Web server for runtime=php. CANONICAL FIELD NAME. Ignored when runtime=node (Traefik proxies straight to node.port). Unknown values fall back to nginx with a warning (validate_project_config).

webserver.description: LEGACY alias for 'server'. Accepted on read; 'server' wins when both are present. Writers MUST NOT emit this. All five pre-v1 PHP projects on disk use this spelling — do not remove read support before they are migrated.

document_root.description: Document root relative to the project directory, for runtime=php. No leading slash, no '..' segments. Ignored when runtime=node.

aliases.description: OPTIONAL. Additional hostnames the same project answers on, beside `domain`. Multi-tenant applications that resolve the tenant from a subdomain cannot be developed with one name; DDEV calls these additional_hostnames and additional_fqdns, Herd allows several per site. A leading `*.` is accepted and becomes a certificate SAN and a Traefik HostRegexp router — but NOT an /etc/hosts entry, because a hosts file cannot express a wildcard. That is a property of the resolver, not a limitation of this field: until StackVo runs a local DNS server (gap E-1), a wildcard alias resolves only for names the user has added by other means, and the app reports it as unresolved rather than pretending otherwise. An entry equal to `domain` is dropped as a duplicate.

lan_share.description: OPTIONAL. Also answer on a name other devices on this network can resolve, so the site can be opened on a real phone. The name is `<project>.<address-with-dashes>.sslip.io` and is DERIVED, never stored here: sslip.io resolves the address out of the name arithmetically, so nothing is registered or published, and a stored name would point at whatever machine took the lease after a laptop changed networks. Only a private (RFC 1918) address is used — on a machine with a public address the switch reports that it cannot help rather than publishing a development site under a name anybody can resolve. The certificate is the local CA's, which the visiting device does not trust, so its browser warns; the connection is real and the name is right, and installing the CA on that device is a manual step the app cannot do for you.

services.description: OPTIONAL. The backing services this project needs, by catalog id — the half of an environment definition that a teammate gets by cloning the repository. The authoritative list of ids is contracts/env.schema.json → services and is deliberately NOT repeated here: two lists of what a service is called is how one of them goes stale. An id this version of StackVo does not know is a WARNING and not an error — the project still builds, and the declaration is reported as unmet rather than silently dropped. NO VERSIONS: a service has exactly one SERVICE_<NAME>_VERSION for the whole workspace, so a project pinning one would silently change every other project's database. project_requirements plans this and project_requirements_apply enables it, through the same plan-then-apply path a preset import uses.

exec.description: Run inside the project's own container. That container already runs the repository's code, so a repository able to run a command in it has gained nothing it did not already have — these need no approval beyond hooks being on.

host.description: Run on the developer's machine, with their files and their credentials. This is the kind that turns `git clone` plus a Start button into arbitrary code execution, so it runs only after the person has read the exact list of commands and approved it — and the approval is recorded against a digest of those commands, so changing one asks again.

items.description: A step is an argv ARRAY, never a command string: nothing in StackVo spawns a shell, and a hook taking shell text would be the one place one came back, holding text from a repository somebody cloned. A step needing a pipeline is a script, and a script is one argv element — ["sh", "scripts/seed.sh"] — which is the user choosing a shell and naming the file rather than the tool deciding every hook is shell. `exec` or `host`, not both: where a step runs is the whole of its risk.

hooks.description: OPTIONAL. Commands to run when this project is rebuilt, started or stopped. `pre-start` is deliberately NOT an event: there is no container to run in before a start, so every pre-start step would have to be a host step — the dangerous kind — and offering a slot whose only possible occupant is the dangerous kind is an invitation rather than a feature. A step that cannot be read is a WARNING and not an error: a typo in an optional convenience must not be the reason a project cannot be opened, so the step does not run and the reason is reported. Steps run in order and stop at the first failure, and a failed hook does NOT fail the start it hangs off — a container that started is started.

php.description: PHP runtime block. MUST be present when runtime is 'php' (or absent). MUST NOT coexist with a 'node' block — the Bash parser reads the first "version" key it finds without disambiguating, so two runtime blocks silently corrupt the generated Dockerfile.

version.description: PHP major.minor. Must be a member of SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_VERSIONS in .env.

xdebug.description: OPTIONAL. Is step debugging switched ON, as distinct from the extension being compiled in. Those are two different things and conflating them cost a rebuild per toggle: `extensions` decides what the image carries, this decides what XDEBUG_MODE the container starts with. Measured: an image carrying Xdebug with mode=off runs at the same speed as one without it (0.009s against 0.009s on a call-heavy benchmark), while mode=debug costs about 6.7x — so leaving the extension compiled in and switching the mode is free when off and takes a container recreate rather than an image rebuild when turned on. Absent means off.

extensions.description: PHP extensions to compile in. See php-extensions.json for install method and system dependencies. There is no count limit: the old HARD LIMIT 50 was the Bash parser's `grep -A 50 '"extensions"'` window (C-04), which retired with the Bash generator — the whole catalog may be selected, at the cost of build time. Omitting this key yields the built-in default set: pdo pdo_mysql mysqli gd curl zip mbstring (get_default_extensions) — which is NOT the same as SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_EXTENSIONS_DEFAULT in .env.

items.description: Lowercase, digits and underscore only. The Bash extractor greps `"[a-z_0-9]*"`, so any uppercase letter or dash makes the extension vanish silently.

node.description: Node runtime block. MUST be present when runtime is 'node'. The key is 'node', NOT 'nodejs' (see CONFLICTS.md C-01).

version.description: Node major version only. Must be a member of SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_NODEJS_VERSIONS in .env.

install.description: Dependency install command, run at image build time.

build.description: Optional build command, run at image build time after install. Omit for projects served straight from source.

start.description: Container entrypoint command. MUST bind 0.0.0.0 (not localhost) on `port`, or Traefik cannot reach it.

package_manager.description: OPTIONAL, and ABSENT IS NOT 'npm'. Absent means the image is built exactly as it always has been: no Corepack line, and `install`/`start` default to the npm spellings. Naming one enables Corepack in the image, which is what makes a `packageManager` field in package.json mean anything — without it that field is a comment and the image installs with whatever version the base image ships. Naming one also changes what `install` and `start` default to (`pnpm install`, `pnpm start`), which an explicit value still overrides. Bun is deliberately not in this list: it is a runtime of its own here, not a way of installing for Node. Corepack ships with Node 16.9 and later; on an older 16.x the RUN line fails the build rather than silently doing nothing.

port.description: Container-internal port Traefik proxies to. Not published on the host.

python.description: Config for one of the six lang runtimes; the key MUST equal the runtime id. Every field is optional — absent fields take the ecosystem defaults (manifest::lang_defaults). An explicitly empty install/build string means 'skip this step', distinct from absent.

go.description: Config for one of the six lang runtimes; the key MUST equal the runtime id. Every field is optional — absent fields take the ecosystem defaults (manifest::lang_defaults). An explicitly empty install/build string means 'skip this step', distinct from absent.

ruby.description: Config for one of the six lang runtimes; the key MUST equal the runtime id. Every field is optional — absent fields take the ecosystem defaults (manifest::lang_defaults). An explicitly empty install/build string means 'skip this step', distinct from absent.

bun.description: Config for one of the six lang runtimes; the key MUST equal the runtime id. Every field is optional — absent fields take the ecosystem defaults (manifest::lang_defaults). An explicitly empty install/build string means 'skip this step', distinct from absent. Bun reads the same package.json scripts Node does; the defaults use Bun's own verbs so the lockfile it writes is the one it reads back.

deno.description: Config for one of the six lang runtimes; the key MUST equal the runtime id. Every field is optional — absent fields take the ecosystem defaults (manifest::lang_defaults). An explicitly empty install/build string means 'skip this step', distinct from absent. `version` MUST be a full patch version (2.9.5, not 2 or 2.9): denoland/deno publishes no major or minor tag, so a shortened one names an image that does not exist. This is the only lang runtime with that constraint, and it is the publisher's, not ours.

rust.description: Config for one of the six lang runtimes; the key MUST equal the runtime id. Every field is optional — absent fields take the ecosystem defaults (manifest::lang_defaults). An explicitly empty install/build string means 'skip this step', distinct from absent.

commands.description: Commands this project offers next to the built-in ones (B-4). The webview still only ever sends an id; what changed is that a workspace may declare one in a file on disk. Keyed by id: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, up to 40 characters. An id that is already a built-in command is refused rather than allowed to replace it, because either silent outcome ends with somebody pressing a button whose label does not describe what it runs.

exec.description: Run inside the project's own container, as an argv ARRAY and never a command string — nothing here spawns a shell to re-split one. There is deliberately no `host` form: a container already runs the repository's code, so a repository able to run a command in it has gained nothing, whereas a host step is what turns a clone plus a button into arbitrary code execution. That one is a hook, where it is approved against a digest first.

about.description: One line shown beside the command.

interactive.description: Needs a TTY and a human at it, like `tinker`. Opens the user's own terminal instead of the operation console.

allOf.$comment: runtime=php (explicit or defaulted) requires the php block and forbids node.
runtime=node requires the node block and forbids php/server/document_root.
'server' and 'webserver' are the same field under two names; emitting both invites drift.

x-stackvo-write-rules.description: Constraints that JSON Schema cannot express but every writer (Bash CLI, Tauri app, humans) MUST honour while the Bash generator remains in the pipeline.

rules.rule: php.extensions MUST be the last key in the document.
rules.why: The Bash extractor greps 50 lines past the "extensions" marker and treats every quoted lowercase token it finds as an extension name. Any key emitted after the array (e.g. "document_root": "public") is swallowed into the extension list and reaches docker-php-ext-install as a bogus name.

rules.rule: Exactly one runtime block (php XOR node) per document.
rules.why: parse_project_config reads "version" with sed and no `head -1`, so a second block produces a multi-line PHP_VERSION and a broken FROM line.

rules.rule: Pretty-print with one array element per line, 2-space indent.
rules.why: Both the extension extractor and the 50-line window are line-oriented. A single-line array is parsed as one token and yields zero extensions.

rules.rule: 'name' MUST equal the parent directory name.
rules.why: listProjects() enumerates directories and keys containers as stackvo-<dirname>; a mismatch makes the project unreachable from the UI.

x-stackvo-read-rules.description: Normalisation every reader MUST apply, in order, before using a manifest.
steps: 2. server: prefer 'server'; fall back to 'webserver'; then .env SUPPORTED_SERVERS_DEFAULT; then 'nginx'.
4. php.version: default .env SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_DEFAULT, then DEFAULT_PHP_VERSION, then '8.2'.
7. domain: no default — a manifest without it is INVALID and MUST be skipped with a user-visible error.
